# 5 — X5D / EXPDB

**A separate subject: analytic number theory proper.** Nothing here is about prime gaps or the wheel.

**The result.** The Tao–Trudgian–Yang Exponent Database is generated by a single polytope $\mathcal P\subset\mathbb R^5$: every entry is a projection or envelope of one shape, with an invariant, a monotone contraction flow and a fixed-point theorem.

**The cusp.** Ingham (1940) and Guth–Maynard (2024) meet at $\sigma=7/10$:
$$\frac{3}{2-\sigma}=\frac{15}{5\sigma+3}=\frac{30}{13},\qquad \theta=1-\frac{13}{30}=\frac{17}{30},\qquad \frac{d\theta}{d\lVert A\rVert}=\frac{169}{900}.$$
The attack surface around it is about 0.006 wide. All four values are exact rationals, asserted by the figure script before drawing.

**Start with the pictures:** [the Guth–Maynard cusp](figures/fig2_guth_maynard_cusp.svg) — where $\theta=17/30$ comes from — and [the dimension ladder](figures/fig1_dimension_ladder.svg), $\mathbb R^5\to\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^1\to\mathbb R^0$: bounds flow down out of $\mathcal P$ by projection, supremum and envelope.
